Name: T's Content Patcher Toolkit
Author: tikamin557
Description:
[center][b][size=5]T's Content Patcher Toolkit[/size][/b]
A standalone Windows toolkit for Content Patcher modding.[/center]
[line]

[color=#00ffff][size=4][b]About[/b][/size][/color]
T's Content Patcher Toolkit is a standalone Windows application designed to provide useful tools for creating and editing Content Patcher mods.

[b][color=#ffff00][size=4]This is not a mod that should be installed in your Stardew Valley Mods folder.[/size][/color][/b]
Simply extract the downloaded ZIP file and run [b]TsCPToolKit.exe[/b].

More tools may be added in future versions as the toolkit is developed.
[line]

[size=4][b][color=#00ffff]Current Features[/color][/b][/size]

[color=#ffff00][b]JSON Indentation[/b][/color]
The main feature of T's Content Patcher Toolkit is a tool for cleaning up the indentation of JSON files used in Content Patcher mods.
Unlike a general JSON formatter, this tool [b]does not rearrange your existing line breaks[/b]. It only adjusts the indentation at the beginning of each line.
For example, if you intentionally write something on a single line:
[code]"Position": { "X": 10, "Y": 20 }[/code]it will remain on a single line.
Likewise, if you intentionally write the same structure across multiple lines:
[code]"Position": {
    "X": 10,
    "Y": 20
}[/code]it will remain across multiple lines.
Multiline values are also preserved and aligned without removing their existing line breaks.
For example:
[code]"Target": "Maps/Example_A,
           Maps/Example_B,
           Maps/Example_C"[/code]The line breaks remain in place, while the continued lines are aligned with the beginning of the value.
This is useful for long Content Patcher fields such as [b]Target[/b], where keeping entries on separate lines can make the file easier to read and edit.
This means you can keep the layout you chose for your Content Patcher files while using the tool to clean up inconsistent or broken indentation.
The contents of each line are preserved, and JSON files containing comments are also supported.

[color=#00ff00][b]Single JSON File[/b][/color]
Select a single JSON file and clean up its indentation.
You can also drag and drop a JSON file directly onto the application window.

[color=#00ff00][b]Folder Batch Processing[/b][/color]
Process all JSON files inside a selected folder at once.
Processing files inside subfolders can also be enabled, which is useful when working with larger Content Patcher mods containing many JSON files.

[color=#00ff00][b]Indentation Size[/b][/color]
Choose the number of spaces used for each indentation level:
[list]
[*]2 spaces[/*]
[*]3 spaces[/*]
[*]4 spaces[/*]
[*]8 spaces[/*]
[/list]
[color=#00ff00][b]Backup[/b][/color]
The application can automatically create backups before modifying JSON files.
[b]Keeping this option enabled is recommended when working with important mod files.[/b]

[b][color=#ffff00]Languages[/color][/b]
The application currently supports:
[list]
[*]English[/*]
[*]Japanese[/*]
[/list]The selected language is saved and restored the next time the application is started.

[b][color=#ffff00]Version Information & Update Check[/color][/b]
The application can check for newer versions when it starts.
If a newer version is available, the version information window will open automatically.
You can also open the version information window manually at any time to check the current and latest available versions.
[line]

[size=4][b][color=#00ffff]Installation[/color][/b][/size]
[b]No installation is required.[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Download the ZIP file.[/*]
[*]Extract it to any location.[/*]
[*]Run [b]TsCPToolKit.exe[/b].[/*]
[/list][b]Do not place the application in your Stardew Valley Mods folder.[/b]
The application is distributed as a standalone Windows executable, so no separate .NET installation is required.
[line]

[color=#00ffff][size=4][b]How to Use[/b][/size][/color]

[b][color=#ffff00]Single JSON File[/color][/b]
[list=1]
[*]Open the [b]Single JSON[/b] tab.[/*]
[*]Select a JSON file using the Browse button, or drag and drop a JSON file onto the application.[/*]
[*]Select your preferred indentation size.[/*]
[*]Choose whether to create a backup.[/*]
[*]Run the indentation process.[/*]
[/list]
[b][color=#ffff00]Folder Batch Processing[/color][/b]
[list=1]
[*]Open the [b]Batch[/b] tab.[/*]
[*]Select the folder containing the JSON files you want to process, or drag and drop the folder onto the application.[/*]
[*]Choose whether JSON files inside subfolders should also be processed.[/*]
[*]Select your preferred indentation size.[/*]
[*]Choose whether to create backups.[/*]
[*]Run the batch process.[/*]
[/list][line]

[color=#00ffff][size=4][b]Important Notes[/b][/size][/color]
This tool is intended to help with editing and organizing Content Patcher JSON files.
It [b]does not validate or repair[/b] incorrect JSON syntax or Content Patcher patches.
The indentation tool is designed to preserve your existing formatting choices wherever possible. It does not intentionally split one-line structures into multiple lines or rearrange the contents of your JSON files.
When working with important files, keeping the backup option enabled is recommended.
[line]

[color=#00ffff][size=4][b]Application Settings[/b][/size][/color]
Application settings are stored in:
[code]Documents
└─ T's Content Patcher Toolkit
   └─ config.json[/code]Deleting [b]config.json[/b] will reset the saved application settings.
